items.title: Stop recurring DNS outages and establish non-destructive recovery
items.observedState: The operator reports five DNS/internet drops on 2026-08-18. The fifth occurrence recovered only after rebooting PVE-PROD-01, the production Proxmox host at 10.10.0.11; NS-01 was not rebooted for that occurrence. At 2026-08-18T20:53:31Z, Office-PC could reach NS-01 and the public internet by IP, but DNS queries to both its configured primary resolver 10.10.0.1 and configured secondary resolver 1.1.1.1 timed out. AdGuard Home is a separate service on NS-01, administered at 10.10.0.1:3000, rather than the OPNsense Unbound resolver. The failure domain and initiating cause are not yet verified.

evidence.source: Operator incident report and read-only Office-PC network snapshot
evidence.summary: Office-PC used static IPv4 10.10.0.100/24, gateway 10.10.0.1, and DNS servers 10.10.0.1 then 1.1.1.1. Four ICMP requests to 10.10.0.1 and four to 1.1.1.1 succeeded with no loss. DNS queries to each resolver timed out, and TCP connectivity to 10.10.0.1:53 failed. The privileged adapter cmdlet was unavailable, so no router, host, service, or packet-level evidence was captured.

evidence.source: Operator clarification in current task
evidence.summary: The fifth outage was recovered by rebooting PVE-PROD-01, the production Proxmox host at 10.10.0.11. The operator also confirmed that AdGuard Home is a separate service on NS-01 at 10.10.0.1:3000 and is not the OPNsense Unbound resolver. Exact outage and reboot timestamps remain needs-capture.

requiredAction: Preserve the DNS/network change freeze until the failure is understood and a reviewed change has exact approval.

Capture timestamped read-only evidence during the next failure from Office-PC, ns-01, and pve-prod-01: resolver process state, listeners, service logs, firewall decisions, interface/link state, resource pressure, packet counters, and upstream reachability.
Determine whether DNS traffic is failing at the client, OPNsense policy/NAT, AdGuard listener/process, Proxmox networking, or upstream path; do not infer causation from recovery after a reboot.
Define a least-disruptive recovery procedure that restores resolution without rebooting the router, hypervisor, or all guests, then validate it only with exact production approval.
Design monitoring and an appropriately independent resolver/recovery path so a single DNS service failure does not silently remove internet access.
acceptanceCriteria: A timestamped incident capture identifies the failed layer before any reboot or restart changes its state.
The verified root cause is supported by router, resolver, hypervisor, and client evidence rather than correlation alone.
A documented least-disruptive recovery restores DNS and is validated without rebooting the router or Proxmox host.
Monitoring distinguishes gateway reachability, raw WAN reachability, local DNS service, external DNS reachability, and application-level resolution.
A reviewed redundancy or fail-safe design prevents one resolver or host failure from causing an unobserved site-wide DNS outage.
items.approvalGate: Read-only observation and local documentation are allowed. No AdGuard, OPNsense, Unbound, DHCP, firewall, route, resolver, Proxmox networking, VM/LXC, DNS-client, or service change/restart/flush is permitted without exact separate approval naming the action and target.
items.rollback: No live mutation is authorized. Preserve current configuration and collect evidence; any later approved change must export the prior configuration and define a tested reversal before execution.
items.externalGate: Root-cause confirmation requires timestamped read-only evidence during a failure and may require operator-approved console or log access.

items.observedState: Cleaner passes its 6 existing local safety/preflight tests, but they do not cover API authorization or the full mutation boundary.
